Hi all,

I'm new to R and knitr but I love the principle and I'm trying to write my first document using R Studio to knit out to a MS Word document. My issue is that any plots I produce have a large amount of whitespace / unused area in the resulting output. 

I could try cropping the image in Word but the image quality doesn't allow me to resize or scale the image

Is the any recommendations for defaults people have found work well with MS Word 2010/2013 for A4 size documents?

I'd appreciate the forums recommendations as my searching to date points to outputting html or Latex using SVG which isn't an option for MS word?

Do most people output the plots to a file and re-insert them into the document later?

Michael

parts:
If you have ImageMagick installed on your system, you can also use it to trim the figures. Here is how I do. I include this chunk at the beginning :

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::knit_hooks$set(trim = function(before, options, envir) {
  if(!before) {
    fig <- knitr::fig_path(".png", num=1) # OK chunk avec un seul plot
    command <- sprintf("convert %s -trim %s", fig, fig)
    system(command)
  }
})
```

Then, use trim=TRUE in the options of your plot chunks.
That should work on Linux if you have ImageMagick installed on your system. On Windows use shell(command) instead of system(command). Your system also has to find the convert command
